subject: MAP: Data access, retention windows & audit trail owners (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Phil Hancock <phil.hancock@medstreamhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Data access, retention windows & audit trail owners (post-call recap)

Phil — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and an initial MAP slice focused on data handling controls so procurement and your compliance team have a concrete starting point. Attaching a one-page MAP draft and a short retention matrix stub.

Key outcomes from the call:
- Scope: inference-only API (tokenized model outputs), customer data in requests may include limited PHI (patient initials, non-identifiable notes) for triage workflows.
- Primary compliance asks: configurable retention windows, immutable audit trails for requests, fine-grained access logs (who queried what), and clear PHI handling exceptions.
- Timeline you asked for: target procurement close by 2026-09-15 if legal review is straightforward.

Proposed MAP milestones (draft):
1) MAP 1.0 — Retention policy & enforcement
   - Owner: Marissa Cole (Redwood)
   - Customer owner: Phil Hancock / MedStream compliance
   - Deliverables: retention config menu (per-workload, per-model), retention default = 30 days, optional long-term = 7 years for regulated records
   - Target completion: 2026-08-28
   - Dependencies: legal sign-off on retention defaults, SOC2 evidence availability

2) MAP 1.1 — Audit logging & export
   - Owner: Rishi Malhotra (Redwood infra)
   - Deliverables: per-token request audit trail, exportable CSV and syslog sink, immutable sequence numbers for tamper-evidence
   - Target completion: 2026-09-04
   - Dependencies: customer syslog endpoint details, agreed retention above

3) MAP 1.2 — PHI handling constraints and isolation
   - Owner: MedStream compliance (customer) + Redwood legal review
   - Deliverables: redlined data flow diagram, contractual addendum for PHI, optional VPC/private deployment quote
   - Target completion: 2026-09-10

Actions for this thread:
- Phil: confirm whether "7 years" is required for any classes of records or just clinical summaries (reply inline).
- Phil/Procurement: share preferred syslog endpoint format and required fields.
- Marissa: update the attached retention_matrix.xlsx with additional MedStream retention categories.
- Rishi: prepare a short note on what we can include in the audit log today vs. roadmap items.

Attachments:
- redwood-MAP-draft-20260818.pdf (MAP one-pager, milestones)
- retention_matrix.xlsx (initial template)

Thanks — I’ll circulate an updated MAP once I have Phil’s answers.

—
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0196

From: Phil Hancock <phil.hancock@medstreamhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medstreamhealth.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Data access, retention windows & audit trail owners (post-call recap)

Monica — appreciate the clear breakdown. A few clarifications from compliance/procurement side: 

1) Retention windows
- Clinical summaries (EHR-derived) must be retained for 7 years per state regs for certain cohorts; other triage logs can be 1 year. Can you model retention by record type?

2) PHI
- We will be treating some inputs as PHI. We need:
  - encryption at rest + in-flight (we assume Redwood supports TLS + KMS).
  - clear contract language about not using customer data for model training.
  - ability to opt into VPC/private deployment if approved later.

3) Audit logs
- Our security policy requires immutable request logs with user identifiers and timestamps. Export via S3 or syslog is fine. We also need a digestible sample CSV to show our auditors.

Procurement timeline: aim remains 2026-09-15 but if legal needs a deeper review (SOC2, ISO), that could slip a week. Can you share SOC2 scope and a pointer to any recent report (redacted ok)?

I’ll loop procurement on specific fields for the syslog. Happy to hop on a short call if it helps.

—
Phil Hancock
Director, IT Security | MedStream Health
phil.hancock@medstreamhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Phil Hancock <phil.hancock@medstreamhealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Data access, retention windows & audit trail owners (post-call recap)

Thanks Phil — noted and good to have the specifics. I’ve taken the draft and itemized owners and short-term deliverables below. I also attached a slightly expanded retention_matrix.xlsx with categories: "clinical_summary", "triage_log", "metadata", "support_record".

Updated assignments (concrete):
- Retention policy engine (Marissa)
  - Task: add per-category retention knobs, UI + API defaults, and an admin override route.
  - Deliverable: retention config spec + API example (openapi snippet).
  - ETA: 2026-08-28 (internal demo to Mon + Phil)

- Audit log exports (Rishi)
  - Task: sample CSV schema + syslog/S3 exporter + immutability header (sequence id + HMAC for tamper detection).
  - Deliverable: sample CSV and a short playbook for ingestion to a SIEM.
  - ETA: 2026-09-04 (deliver to procurement/security)

- Contract/Training clause (Legal/Monica to coordinate)
  - Task: redline that data will not be used for model training; confirm KMS integration options.
  - Deliverable: one-page addendum for legal review.
  - ETA: initial draft 2026-08-25

Dependencies and risks:
- SOC2 evidence: Monica, can you share the SOC2 summary link (redacted) and indicate whether it covers our audit logging feature?
- If MedStream requires private deployment (VPC/on-prem), we’ll need procurement to approve a quote — this adds 2–3 weeks.

Next steps I’ll run today:
- Attach retention_matrix.xlsx (updated).
- Rishi to post the sample CSV to the Drive folder.
- Monica to push SOC2 summary pointer and update the MAP PDF with dates above.

Let me know if any of the ETAs are too optimistic and we’ll adjust.

—
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: retention_matrix.xlsx

Phil — great, thanks for the detail. Quick notes and confirmations below (and I updated the MAP PDF in Drive with the exact milestones/owners Marissa listed).

- SOC2: attaching a redacted SOC2_summary_link.txt (link to our compliance page + statement of scope). This covers the hosting and logging controls (desktop and API layers) but we’ll confirm the exact controls Rishi references when he posts the CSV sample.
- Retention: we will expose per-category retention; default set to 30 days for non-clinical and 7 years option for clinical_summary. We’ll include the API shown in the spec for enforcement and an admin override flow for compliance teams.
- PHI & Training: Redwood confirms no customer data will be used for model training unless explicitly opted-in and contractually agreed. I’ll coordinate a one-page addendum and send initial redlines by 2026-08-25.
- Next meeting: propose a 30-minute sync the week of 2026-08-31 to review the retention demo and CSV sample. Does 2026-09-01 10:00 AM PT work for you?

Phil — can you confirm the 7-year requirement applies to "clinical_summary" only (reply yes/no)? Procurement, if you have the syslog field list, please paste it in a reply and we’ll match the sample CSV.

If all good I’ll convert this MAP slice into the canonical HubSpot attachment and tag the deal as "MAP in progress".

Thanks —
Monica
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
